posts.content: 期刊論文：分析 6–17 個月嬰兒家居錄影，誇張表情原型日常極少出現；就算只計全臉時間，快樂表情都只佔 12%。
posts.title: Infants' facial input from 6 to 17 months rarely includes hypothesized expressive emotion prototypes (Communications Psychology 2026; DOI: 10.1038/s44271-026-00539-z)

summary_en: Published in Communications Psychology in 2026 (DOI: 10.1038/s44271-026-00539-z; published 24 September 2026, press coverage 17 November 2026). A University of Kansas team analysed a longitudinal corpus of home video recordings of infants aged 6 to 17 months (SEEDLingS data), one hour per month. Infants were mostly exposed to partial faces rather than full faces; even within full-face time, the most common happiness prototype accounted for only 12%. The exaggerated expressions used in laboratory research (big toothy smiles, scowls, exaggerated frowns) were extremely rare in everyday life, and when they did occur they often appeared in unexpected contexts, not necessarily carrying the presumed emotional meaning. The authors argue infants learn emotion from the whole context, not from one-to-one mappings between facial configurations and emotion categories.
summary_zh: Communications Psychology 2026 年刊出（DOI: 10.1038/s44271-026-00539-z；2026 年 9 月 24 日刊出，11 月 17 日新聞報導）。堪薩斯大學團隊分析 6–17 個月大嬰兒嘅縱向家居錄影（SEEDLingS 數據），每月一小時。結果：嬰兒多數見到半邊臉，唔係成塊臉；就算只計見到成塊臉嘅時間，最常見嘅快樂原型表情都只佔 12%；實驗室用開嘅誇張表情（大笑、怒目、誇張皺眉）日常極少出現，而且出現嗰陣處境往往出乎意料，未必代表預設嘅情緒意思。作者指出，嬰兒學情緒唔係靠一對一認表情，而係靠成個處境同學習過程。
supervision_questions: 你用開嘅情緒識別圖卡，係咪都係誇張表情？如果換成日常自然表情，教學上要點調整？
